newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: SOLO YACHTSMEN RETURNING TO LAND
The two solo yachtsmen plucked to safety out of the Southern Ocean off Western Australia this morning, are expected to arrive in Perth by Sunday or Monday.
Briton Tony Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois spent four days awaiting rescue after their yachts capsized in treacherous seas off Western Australia.
They are both currently recovering from their ordeals aboard the Navy frigate, HMAS Adelaide, which is headed towards Perth.
Meanwhile one of the designers of Mr Bullimore's yacht, Martin Smith, says it's a miracle the lone sailor was found alive.
Speaking from England, Mr Smith said the vessel was designed with special bouyancy materials to ensure it did not sink in the event of it capsizing.
He says his main concern was that Mr Bullimore had NOT been able to make it into the cabin before it capsized.
RACE ORGANISER DEFENDS SOLO YACHT ROUTE
Despite today's dramatic rescues of two solo yachtsmen, the organiser of the Vendee Global Challenge, denies the route taken in the round the world race is to blame.
Phillipe Jeantot was responding to veteran British yachtsman Chay Blyth who says competitors should take a more northerly route to avoid the treacherous southern seas.
British sailor Tony Bullimore was rescued from his overturned yacht earlier today after four days in icy waters 14-hundred nautical miles south west of Perth.
And French yachtsman Thierry Dubois was rescued by a navy helicopter this morning, after his four-day ordeal in the Southern Ocean.
Mr Jeantot says while he's willing to consider changing the course, it won't make any difference, as life-threatening seas can be experienced anywhere.
Mr Blythe says if the organisers are going to stick to the route they need to change the rules for the minimum yacht size.
OPPOSITION CONCERNS OVER POPULATION LEVEL
The Federal Opposition has expressed concern that Australia's population will fall without continued migration.
Labor is supporting a formal population policy for Australia.
Shadow Immigration Minister, Duncan Kerr, has called on the Government to start discussions on a formal policy - based on economic, social and environmental concerns.
Mr Kerr won't say what the population target should be, except to rule out a figure as high as 200-million or any rapid population fall.
He says there would be problems if the population fell.
PACEMAKER RECIPIENTS CONFIDENT OF SUCCESS IN LEGAL CLAIM
Australians who believe they received faulty heart pacemaker leads from Pacific Dunlop are preparing to serve a class action against the industrial group.
Lawyers for the close to 12-hundred people involved in the legal action say they're confident of success.
The industrial group will soon be served with a claim from users, who say the leads have broken, causing potentially life-threatening complications.
A similar action is already underway in Canada, while several hundred people have filed individual claims in the United States.
CHARGES LIKELY AFTER RETRIBUTION ATTACKS
Police at Fitzroy Crossing in Western Australia's Kimberley region expect to lay charges against several people involved in a traditional Aboriginal "payback" that has left two men in hospital.
One man is in a Perth Hospital with serious head injuries, the other has since been released after receiving fractured limbs and severe bruising.
The men, in their 20s, were invited to the Bayulu community in December to discuss the recent death of a 23-year-old woman, who died in a hit and run accident east of the town.
Senior Sergeant Roy Bracknell, of Fitzroy Crossing Police, says the men were met by about 500 people when they arrived at the community, and the situation "got out of hand".
He says some Aboriginal Elders were concerned the payback was not carried out in accordance with traditional methods, and have asked police to investigate.
VIETNAMESE FAMILY DENY THEY PROVOKED ASSAULT
A Vietnamese couple from Sydney who were kicked and beaten outside a Surfers' Paradise service station earlier this week, say they did nothing to provoke their assault.
In a Gold Coast newspaper today, the man who claims he assaulted Loi Dao and his wife Huong says "they deserved what they got."
The alleged attacker, who only used his first name "Tony", told the Gold Coast Bulletin Mr Dao had provoked the attack by sexually assaulting his girlfriend.
But Mr Dao says he and his family are still very distressed and upset about the incident especially since he did nothing to trigger the attack.
CHAMBER SUPPORTS FORD'S STANCE ON TARIFFS
The Australian Business Chamber has backed Ford's call for tariffs in the car industry to stay at 15 per cent until at least 2005.
The Industry Commission's recommended that tariffs be lowered to five percent by the start of 2005.
The Ford motor Company has warned it might drastically cut Australian production if the Federal Government accepts the Commission's recommendation.
The Business Chamber says cutting tariffs to the recommended levels would ignore the importance of the industry to the Australian economy, and in particular the regions where it's concentrated.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
